title: Consumer Credit Stress
headline_read: Consumer credit bears watching — debt loads are creeping up.

indicators.title: Credit-Card Delinquency Rate
indicators.context: The share of bank credit-card balances 30+ days past due (quarterly). Cards go bad first — this is the earliest warning in consumer credit. The 2009 peak was about 6.8%.
indicators.read: Credit-card delinquencies are at 2.9%, creeping up off their lows.

indicators.title: Consumer-Loan Delinquency Rate
indicators.context: Delinquency across all consumer loans at banks — cards, autos, and personal loans together (quarterly).
indicators.read: Consumer-loan delinquencies are at 2.6%, creeping up off their lows.

indicators.title: Card Balances · year-over-year
indicators.context: How fast revolving credit (mostly credit cards) is growing. Balances growing much faster than incomes mean households are borrowing to keep up.
indicators.read: Card balances are growing 3.8% a year — a sustainable pace.

indicators.title: Household Debt Service · % of income
indicators.context: All required debt payments — mortgage and consumer — as a share of disposable income (quarterly). The 2007 peak was about 13%.
indicators.read: Debt payments take 11.2% of household income — above the comfortable range.

indicators.title: New-Car Loan Rate · 48-month
indicators.context: What banks charge on a 48-month new-car loan (quarterly, since 1972) — the interest rate households actually meet when they finance a car, as opposed to the Treasury rates markets watch.
indicators.read: The average new-car loan rate is 7.5%, little changed from a year ago.
indicators.no_severity_reason: A retail borrowing rate shown for context — the scored consumer-stress reads here are delinquencies, balances, and debt service.
